subject.title: Concurrent message handling per session (async agent turns)

question: Which same-session responsiveness model should OpenClaw support when a new message arrives during an active long-running turn?
rationale: The source-level problem is real, but changing it crosses transcript ordering, tool side effects, session write ownership, public config shape, and rate-limit policy, which cannot be safely inferred from code alone.

options.title: Prefer one-writer steer/yield model
options.body: Preserve one active writer per session and improve admission so urgent or short messages steer, interrupt, or yield at safe runtime boundaries.

options.title: Add opt-in fast-lane concurrency
options.body: Introduce a bounded parallel-turn mode only behind explicit config with safety tests and real channel proof.

options.title: Consolidate under umbrella issue
options.body: Treat the broader concurrency/config/autoyield work as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53023 and close narrower duplicates after maintainer confirmation.

recommendation.title: Prefer one-writer steer/yield model
recommendation.body: Preserve one active writer per session and improve admission so urgent or short messages steer, interrupt, or yield at safe runtime boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits in the command queue, reply runner, and config surface where history shows the strongest ownership signal.
